title: Novel Histomorphometrical Approach to Evaluate the Integration Pattern and Functionality of Barrier Membranes
authors: Ottenbacher N, Alkildani S, Korzinskas T, Pissarek J, Ulm C, Jung O, Sundag B, Bellmann O, Stojanovic S, Najman S, Zechner W, Barbeck M. Dent J (Basel). 2021 Oct;9(11):127. doi: 10.3390/dj9110127.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss Jason membrane (porcine pericardium) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Abstract, verbatim (no separate conclusion section): “GBR (guided bone regeneration) is a standard procedure for building up bony defects in the jaw. In this procedure, resorbable membranes made of bovine and porcine collagen are increasingly being used, which, in addition to many possible advantages, could h ave the potential disadvantage of a shorter barrier functionality, especially when augmenting large -volume defects. Thus, it is of importance to evaluate the integration behavior and especially the standing time of barrier membranes using specialized methods to predict its respective biocompatibility. This study is intended to establish a new histomorphometrical analysis method to quantify the integration rate of collagen-based barrier membranes.
